children: DISA Uranium deployed its HPSA technology at Mary Ann in Colorado, its first abandoned uranium mine cleanup under its U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission Service Provider License. American Atomics holds a net smelter return royalty on minerals recovered under their agreement.
DISA's first NRC-licensed cleanup is at Mary Ann
The field deployment advances the partnership beyond agreement into operating experience; recovery and commercial results remain unreported.
American Atomics holds a net smelter return royalty
The company can participate in value from minerals sold, but the release gives no recovery volumes, sales, or royalty estimates.
Further deployments depend on approvals and economics
Expansion across the portfolio is conditional, so the release does not establish a repeatable revenue stream.

This is an early field demonstration under an agreement announced in July 2025, rather than confirmation of commercial-scale recovery. Evidence of recovered and sold minerals, quantified royalty proceeds, or approved deployments at additional sites would be needed to make it a larger catalyst.
